millimeter.definition: A metric unit of length equal to one thousandth of a meter.

centimeter.definition: A metric unit of length equal to one hundredth of a meter.

meter.definition: A metric unit of length equal to one hundred centimeters.

kilometer.definition: A metric unit of length equal to 1000 meters (or 0.621371 miles).

inch.definition: A unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot.

foot.definition: The part of the leg of a human being below the ankle joint.

yard.definition: The enclosed land around a house or other building.

mile.definition: A unit of length used in navigation.

ruler.definition: A straight tool used for measuring and drawing lines.
ruler.exampleUsage: The ruler was used during the activity.

tape-measure.definition: A flexible strip used for measuring length.

gram.definition: A metric unit of weight equal to one thousandth of a kilogram.

kilogram.definition: A metric unit of mass equal to one thousand grams.

ton.definition: A United States unit of weight equivalent to 2000 pounds.

ounce.definition: A unit of apothecary weight equal to 480 grains or one twelfth of a troy pound.

pound.definition: A nontechnical unit of force equal to the mass of 1 pound with an acceleration of free fall equal to 32 feet/sec/sec.

stone.definition: An avoirdupois unit used to measure the weight of a human body.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

balance.definition: Harmonious arrangement or relation of parts or elements within a whole (as in a design).

heavy.definition: Unusually great in degree or quantity or number.

milliliter.definition: A metric unit of volume equal to one thousandth of a liter.

liter.definition: A metric unit of capacity, formerly defined as the volume of one kilogram of pure water under standard conditions.

gallon.definition: A British imperial capacity measure (liquid or dry) equal to 4 quarts or 4.545 liters.

quart.definition: A United States liquid unit equal to 32 fluid ounces.

pint.definition: A United States liquid unit equal to 16 fluid ounces.

tablespoon.definition: As much as a tablespoon will hold.

teaspoon.definition: As much as a teaspoon will hold.

fluid-ounce.definition: A British imperial measure of volume can be used for liquids or dry materials. It equals eight fluid drams, or 28.416 cubic centimetres, which is 1.734 cubic inches.

barrel.definition: The quantity that a barrel (of any size) will hold.

celsius.definition: Swedish astronomer who devised the centigrade thermometer (1701-1744).

fahrenheit.definition: Of or relating to a temperature scale proposed by the inventor of the mercury thermometer.

kelvin.definition: British physicist who invented the Kelvin scale of temperature and pioneered undersea telegraphy (1824-1907).

degree.definition: A unit of temperature on a specified scale.

boiling-point.definition: The temperature at which a liquid changes into gas under a stated pressure, commonly the pressure of air at sea level.

freezing-point.definition: The temperature at which a liquid becomes a solid under specified conditions.
freezing-point.exampleUsage: Water has a freezing point of about zero degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure.

body-temperature.definition: The amount of heat inside a living organism, determined by taking a thermometer reading.

room-temperature.definition: Describes a substance or condition at the usual indoor temperature, without deliberate cooling or heating.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer was used during the activity.

heat.definition: A form of energy that is transferred by a difference in temperature.

second.definition: A part or voice or instrument or orchestra section lower in pitch than or subordinate to the first.
second.exampleUsage: The second was used during the activity.

minute.definition: A unit of time equal to 60 seconds or 1/60th of an hour.

hour.definition: A period of time equal to 1/24th of a day.

day.definition: A point or period in time.

speed.definition: A rate (usually rapid) at which something happens.

acceleration.definition: An increase in rate of change.

distance.definition: The amount of space between two places or objects.

rate.definition: A magnitude or frequency relative to a time unit.
